title: Adaptive SLO-driven isolation playbook for Private/Dedicated deployments
creator: Marco R. Santos
description: Create an operational and technical playbook that enables SLO-driven, adaptive tenant isolation and multi-region failover for Dedicated and Private control planes. The goal is to contain noisy/overloaded tenants with minimal collateral impact, preserve critical SLOs for other tenants, and provide safe upgrade/rollout primitives that reduce blast radius during maintenance. This ticket covers design, implementation hooks in the control plane, circuit-breaker algorithms tied to error-budget burn, load-shedding policies at the serving runtime, and an incident runbook with automated mitigations and manual escalation paths.
decision_log: 2026-03-02: Choose SLO-first rather than static resource thresholds — primary signal will be error budget burn rate and p99 latency over short and long windows.
2026-03-04: Use soft-isolation tier (throttling + prioritized queueing) as default; escalate to hard-isolation (placement eviction/tenant fencing) only when burn-rate > 5x sustained for 3 minutes.
2026-03-06: Circuit breakers will operate on per-tenant and per-route keys; breaker state stored in control plane with TTL-backed local cache on serving nodes to minimize control-plane chattiness.

2026-03-08: Multi-region failover uses pre-authorized standby regions with warmed model checkpoints and KV-cache seeding to reduce cold-start impact; failover policy supports staggered fan-out and sticky session preservation when possible.
acceptance_criteria: Design doc reviewed and approved by Reliability and Private infra (link to doc in comments).
Implementation exposes per-tenant error-budget metrics and a computed isolation-score available via control plane API.
Circuit breaker prototype implemented and validated in canary with synthetic tenants showing expected open/half-open/close transitions.
Load-shedding policy integrated with runtime so that high-throughput tenants get prioritized until their isolation threshold is reached.
Upgrade safety: staged rollout with tenant-scoped fencing is exercised on a non-prod stack and rollback path is tested.
Runbook documented and exercised in a game day; metrics and dashboards created for on-call.
No customer-facing incidents during a targeted canary failover test across two regions (metrics within defined SLOs).
implementation_plan: Phase 1 (design): finalize SLO math, isolation-score function, and breaker thresholds. Owner: Leah Chen. Due: 2026-03-10.
Phase 2 (control plane): add isolation-score API, persistent breaker state, and tenant priority flags. Owner: Reliability infra. Estimated: 2 weeks.
Phase 3 (serving runtime): implement soft-isolation throttles, queue prioritization, and a fast local cache for breaker state. Owner: Serving runtime team. Estimated: 2 weeks.
Phase 4 (failover): pre-authorize standby regions, add KV-cache seeding job, and a staged failover orchestrator. Owner: Multi-region ops. Estimated: 3 weeks.
Phase 5 (QA & canary): run controlled experiments with synthetic noisy tenants, measure isolation effectiveness and collateral SLO impact. Owner: SRE/QA.
Phase 6 (rollout): gradual rollout to Dedicated customers then Private early-adopters with opt-in, monitor for regressions.
qa_plan: Synthetic tenant generator to simulate CPU-bound, token-heavy, and latency-sensitive workloads.
Failure injection: simulate control plane latency and control-plane datastore partition to validate local cache and TTL behavior.
Chaos tests: sudden 10x request spike from a single tenant while others run steady workloads to validate isolation and p99 guarantees.
Canary failover: shift a subset of tenant traffic to standby region and validate KV cache seeding and model loading times.
Regression checks: ensure billing and observability telemetry are intact after isolation events.
monitoring_metrics: per-tenant request error rate (4xx/5xx) and model-runtime exceptions
breaker state transitions (count of opens, half-opens, closes)
control plane API latency for isolation-score queries
region failover time and cold-start delays (model load + KV cache restore)
percentage of requests served in soft-isolation vs hard-isolation
runbook_steps: Alert fires: error-budget-burn > 3x baseline for 2m (automated). On-call acknowledges and checks per-tenant isolation-score dashboard.
If single-tenant is cause: apply soft-isolation profile (throttle 50%, deprioritize background batches) via control plane toggle and monitor for SLO improvements.
If soft-isolation not effective after 3 minutes and burn-rate > 5x: escalate to hard-isolation fencing which gracefully drains and quarantines the tenant from overloaded capacity pools.

If multiple tenants across a region show correlated burn: begin staged region failover to pre-authorized standby using orchestrator; warm model checkpoints first, then migrate traffic in 2-minute batches.
If control plane degraded: enable local TTL-based breaker cache on serving nodes and switch to degraded-mode where decisions are based on last-known isolation-scores.
Post-incident: capture timeline, root cause, and metrics; run postmortem and follow-up action items for tuning thresholds and improving observability.
